A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRADATE despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-classification experiments on six datasets under density and size shifts, alongside empirical runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds label-free selection evaluations, additional model evaluations and molecular-dataset runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The LinearFGW distances, GDD objective, GREAT weight updates and sparse projection, and GRADATE procedure in Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged. Setting c=0 was already supported in v1; the proposed node-level extension remains future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six datasets and graph-density and graph-size shifts. v1 already includes unsupervised GDA with c=0. Additional backbones and runtime measurements do not introduce new dataset or task coverage, and node-level adaptation is not evaluated.

E2.justification: The original named comparators remain. G.8 describes A2GNN-ADV, A2GNN-MMD and TDSS as additional models enhanced by GRADATE against other selectors, whereas Table 11's caption describes comparisons against those GDA methods. Reporting only relative gains over an unidentified strongest baseline leaves unclear whether comparator membership changed or existing selectors were tested with additional models.

E3.justification: G.6–G.8 add a dedicated c=0 evaluation, SGFormer and APPNP backbones, and additional GDA configurations. The new comparisons report relative percentage improvements over the strongest baseline. Existing splits, accuracy/AUCROC metrics, training budgets and original model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: G.6 adds an explicit validation-label-signal ablation using GCN and GIN across selection ratios. Appendix M extends the existing runtime analysis to the three OGB datasets, including the larger ogbg-molhiv dataset. These are targeted extensions of the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over 3–5 random trials for classification results. However, new Tables 9–11 present relative improvements without uncertainty estimates, unlike the retained classification tables. No increased run count or new statistical test is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 9–11 add substantial findings for label-free selection and additional models, including losses such as TDSS's -42.10% on IMDB-MULTI. Table 14 adds OGB runtime results. Existing Tables 1–8 retain their values except that Table 5 fills the previously blank full-data GAT result on ogbg-molhiv with 0.571±0.030; these additions are not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, complexity Proposition 3.5, and Appendix F assumptions and proofs are substantively unchanged. Differences concern citation numbering and pagination.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about FGW guarantees, GDD, model-free selection, data efficiency and enhancing GDA methods. Additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 and G.6 expand discussion of label-signal tuning and validation-label availability. New limitation N.4 discusses possible node-level adaptation through ego-graphs and unresolved neighborhood-size, node/edge-selection and information-loss issues. The earlier three limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Table 14 newly documents molecular-dataset preprocessing, selection and GCN training runtimes. The added checklist states a commitment to provide code during submission and upon acceptance, without establishing an accessible release. Existing hardware, implementation and hyperparameter descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussion of TMD-based graph subsampling, A2GNN, TDSS and pairwise alignment. New Appendix L adds broader graph-learning and optimal-transport references. This expands contextual coverage while retaining the original model-free, data-centric positioning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with localized explanatory additions, new appendix subsections, acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the revision is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–11 and 14, including compact relative-improvement displays. The existing dataset-statistics and runtime tables become Tables 12 and 13, while the ECDF figures remain unchanged. Front-page author placement, captions and page flow receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added label-signal ablation, model evaluations and OGB timings provide useful checks of existing applicability and efficiency claims while preserving the original evidence. Gains are limited by missing uncertainty and comparator detail in the new tables, and overstated interpretations: Table 11 includes negative improvements, while Table 14 reports 295.42 seconds for selection versus 312.08 seconds for GCN training at 20% on ogbg-molhiv, despite describing selection overhead as negligible.
